# Performance ledger (perf-ledger)

> A standing ledger that holds the **filing, adoption decisions, kill criteria and relative priority among candidates** of performance
> candidates. The canonical source for measured values is each snapshot in `docs/research/` — this ledger does not copy numbers
> but points to the source (when it does write a number, it always adds the date). **The canonical source for the phase order and
> status of the whole project is [backlog](backlog.md)** — this ledger only rules within the performance candidates (no double
> ledger).
> Status: ✅ done / 🚧 planned (not yet done) / 🧪 experimental (adoption as the default undecided) /
> ❌ rejected (kept as a record).
> Do not write open TODOs in ✅ / ❌ rows — remaining work is filed in backlog and pointed to.
> Origin of the filing: the D4 leg of the 2026-08-12 exhaustive review (`.claude/reviews/2026-08-12_faef828/findings/D4.md`
> — not tracked by git, so the decision part was moved into this ledger. The old `.claude/reviews/PERFORMANCE.md` is frozen as a
> point-in-time snapshot). The origin of H-5 / H-6 / K-8 / K-9 / L-4 to L-6 is the external review of
> 2026-08-13 (`.claude/reviews/2026-08-13_chatgpt-reviews/` — not tracked by git, so the numbers needed for the decisions were
> copied into this ledger with their dates).

## Policy (the role of the bit-identity check — standing)

> **The role of the bit-identity check (the maintainer's policy 2026-08-13): it is an indicator that the implementation is
> correct, not a goal in itself.** Optimisations that change numbers are allowed as an **opt-in option** — default =
> the reference path (the sha256 checks are frozen there and kept as the indicator); the opt-in side gets an A/B band check against the
> reference path + census; a quality ruling is made only when promoting it to the default (making w8a8 the default is the precedent). **Division of
> quality control (supplement of the same day): the correctness and non-destructiveness of the implementation are verified mechanically with bit identity,
> and the parts where bit identity is not guaranteed are quality-controlled by human review (listening, viewing)** — even when the numbers are much worse,
> the generated result often has not collapsed, so human evaluation takes precedence over numeric indicators (the precedent is "listening
> beats LSD 5.64" when w8a8 became the default). This policy replaces the old "designing a substitute quality check is the precondition". The
> first step of the 2026-08-12 ruling (no preconditions) is done.

2026-09-26: the acceptance contract of the reference path / practical presets is [ADR 0110](decisions/0110-practical-tier-numerics-contract.md)
(contract classes E / C / R / Q, the four-point kernel check, in-device determinism MUST for the practical presets too, sha reference-path rows / practical-preset rows).
Approximate kernels (Q) come in under this contract.

Performance waves ① to ③ of the 2026-08-13 ruling are **done** (wave ① K-4a = ADR 0053 / wave ② the H group = ADR 0054 /
wave ③ K-5 = ADR 0058 and 0060, closed on 2026-08-14 — the history is in each ADR and in research).
From then on, the canonical source for the phase order and open items is [backlog](backlog.md) (this section holds no order).
Ordering constraints among candidates stay in each row's preconditions column (e.g. K-4b after H-4).

In the follow-up investigation of 2026-09-10, residency of Anima's fixed inputs alone could not show an overall gain, and the idea of excluding MTP's first W1 observation
had no stable improvement across 10 conditions either; neither was adopted. Deno's asynchronous map wait was attributed to an internal sleep of the runtime version.
See [the host measurements](research/2026-09-10-codex-mtp-optimization.md#ホスト待ちと既存融合の追加測定) and
[the W1 results](research/2026-09-10-codex-mtp-optimization.md#独立した公式-cpu-検証で停止2209-utc-頃).
This does not mean that latent / scheduler residency or new gate designs were rejected. The remaining work is in backlog.

The accumulation fits in int32 with the current K and value range. It is a new kernel with a different contract from the existing w4a8 ([ADR 0076](decisions/0076-w4a8-linear-execution.md)), and it ripples into the WGSL, estimates, fusion and tests. kill criterion: rejected if the spike measurement gains neither "an improvement in the sequence match rate with the official mobile" nor "speed". It changes the numbers of the default path, so it comes with updates of the bit-identity checks and the goldens. **2026-09-19 refutation** ([decode speed investigation](research/2026-09-19-qat-speed-recon.md) §9 cluster C): the expected gain is 0.9 ms/token of GPU (about half of the estimate at filing, including the GEMV efficiency ideas H1 / H2). The kill decision of step 0 comes first (no new kernel needed — a standalone A/B of a comparison shader that replaces only the multiply-add expansion with the minimal instruction form; rejected if under 25% on i2 262144×1536). The implementation point is inside the linear→SRQ fusion kernel (Route A: unpack the weight word → −z → pack4xI8 → dot4I8Packed, no row sums needed / Route B: unsigned dot product + activation bias a^0x80 + 2 correction terms in the epilogue). dot4U8Packed / dot4I8Packed have the same signedness on both sides, so the mixed form "unsigned weights × signed activations" cannot be written as is. **Step 0 passed (2026-09-19, research §14)**: on the occupancy-saturated lm_head shape the minimal instruction form is 2.1 times, on the gate/up shape 2.7 times, past the check. But the bottleneck is not the ALU but **the number of activation loads** (down shape 83% / i4 g512 48% / gate and up 41%, arithmetic 0.3% / 8% / 23%, only lm_head 36%), and the arithmetic of `dot4I8Packed` itself is free. The shape of step 1 needs a decision: packed int8 activations + the current f32 FMA (portable) first, and the integer dot product only for the lm_head shape. **Step 1a implemented** (`57416eb` + follow-up, ADR 0105, option `packedStaticQuantize` default false, u32 match on every shape, id sequences match). A/B (research §16): packing only the 4 shapes that measured effective (K length × lanes 32) gives **Chrome +8.3% / GPU −0.57 ms/token, Deno +1.5 to 2.9%** (packing every shape cancels out through insufficient occupancy of the SRQ kernel and worse lanes 2/4 shapes). **2026-09-20**: declared in `i4-fast` (ADR 0105 addendum 2, an option in hub's SessionSpec + distribution rebuild). M2 follow-up = speed-neutral (35.8 / 35.9 tok/s); at first the id sequences of the English prompt diverged between off/on → the cause was how Metal contracts fma, and fixing the parallel GEMV family to explicit fma made the id sequences match (ADR 0105 addendum 4, research §16.1). **Step 1b is rejected**: the real model's lm_head has no int8 activations (the SRQ scale of the official checkpoint is 0 = identity, so the recipe does not insert it), the upper bound is 36% arithmetic of lm_head's 0.24 ms/token ≈ 0.09 ms (1.3% of the GPU), and going integer would need dynamic quantisation that the official one does not have either (the same decision as K-52) **2026-11-03 — implemented as the integer GEMV** ([ADR 0140](decisions/0140-integer-gemv.md), opt-in `integerGemv`, which requires `packedStaticQuantize`; declared by no preset): exact integer sums per group (lane sums in f32 within 2^24, an i32 tree), the scales applied once in a fixed epilogue, mirror class E (692 / 692 cases on the M2). Not the `dot4I8Packed` route above: on the M2 the GEMV is bound by the per-element weight decode, so the decode is a byte-plane `unpack4x8unorm` with a per-step round ([research 2026-11-03](research/2026-11-03-qat-integer-gemv-m2.md)). M2 / Chrome, QAT E2B greedy (2026-11-03): 27.767 → 22.754 / 27.835 → 22.768 ms/token (×0.820 / ×0.818); by an A / B / B / A attribution the i2 shapes (the shared gate / up and down) alone give 4.143 / 3.263 ms and the i4 shapes (o 2048 / o 4096 / the own-KV down) add 0.93 / 1.68 ms; the i4 shapes at K = 1536 and the i8 PLE shapes were not faster and are not eligible. The GPU tests on the RTX 3080 Ti and the sha rows are pending; default adoption is undecided (ADR 0110 §8) |
| 🚧     | K-46 | int8 KV cache for QAT (official `k_cache_scale` / `v_cache_scale`, staged plan = full layers only) | Precondition: the official checkpoint has a fixed scale per layer. The full layers alone take most of the gain (E2B 32k 384 → 96 MiB). The sliding layers are a fixed buffer of window 512 and can stay out of scope. Comes with extending the dtype of the states form (generation-context / state-attention / estimates / the states conversion of exporter). kill criterion: not started while the product's target context length stays at a few thousand. int8 KV changes the numbers, so it is rejected if quality drops. **2026-09-19 refutation** ([decode speed investigation](research/2026-09-19-qat-speed-recon.md) §7.2 / cluster K): it does not help decode speed (at L≈100 the KV path is 0.15 ms/token, and even at 16k context attention is latency-bound, so the "bandwidth-bound" start condition does not hold) — **taken out of the speed phase and treated as an item about memory and the capacity ceiling** (KV 60 → 15 MiB at capacity 4096, 1,548 → 387 MiB at 131k, the binding limit of the full slots relaxes 4 times). sliding reads 24,576 B per position, twice the full layers, so the staged plan of "full only" is dropped and both are done at once. There is no scale collision on shared slots (the `k/v_cache_scale` of shared layers match the source; `v_cache_scale` is suspected not to be calibrated per layer). Start after a quality acceptance for contexts beyond 512 is in place                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 🚧     | K-47 | Scale duplication caused by `group_size` being required for `i4` (E2B 2.4 MB / E4B 16.7 MiB)       | Precondition: QAT's fixed I4 fills in by duplicating the upstream per-row scale for the number of groups. The value is fully constant within a row, so the numbers do not change, but the distribution bytes and residency grow purely, and GEMV / GEMM fetch the scale again for every word. Resolving it needs a format change that allows a per-row scale (without `group_size`) for `i4` as for `i2`. kill criterion: rejected if a reduction of about 0.78% of the 2.25 GB E4B distribution is not worth the ripple into IR, exporter, every i4 kernel, the WGSL snapshots and the published assets. That hoisting may break bit identity is the same point as i8 in [ADR 0019](decisions/0019-i8-weight-execution.md). **2026-09-19 refutation** ([decode speed investigation](research/2026-09-19-qat-speed-recon.md) cluster H2): rejected as a speed idea — an i4 word = 32 elements, so scale reads are only 48 per column, and K-45 takes the effect of folding ZP and scale into the epilogue without a format change. Kept only as a distribution-size item The evidence is the [decode speed investigation](research/2026-09-19-qat-speed-recon.md) (cost model, refutations and order in §9 to 10). The current state on Chrome is a wall of 10.03 ms / GPU 6.79 ms after ADR 0103 (2026-09-25 note: after the packed activations of ADR 0105 the GPU is 6.63 ms — in a different measurement round with a baseline of 7.20 ms, [research §16](research/2026-09-19-qat-speed-recon.md)). Gains are marginal values when combined (ms/token).

## 2026-09-24 additional candidates from the whole-codebase review

The evidence is the performance ruling FB3 and the top 10 speed-up ideas of the 2026-09-24 whole-codebase review (HEAD `569249ac`) (`.claude/reviews/2026-09-24_569249ac/fable/FB3-performance.md` —
not tracked by git, so the numbers needed for the decisions were copied into this section with their dates). All hold; no regression to fix before 0.13.0 (all are structural costs).
Numbers labelled "speculation" are unmeasured estimates. Existing rows extended by the same review: H-7 (irodori's weight), H-10 (the population behind 1.7µs),
H-14 (idea rank 6), K-22 (idea rank 4), H-28 (correction of the TTFT attribution — the addendum to research 2026-09-19 §15.2).

## 2026-10-10 seams in Wan's DiT passes (from the maintainer's observation)

The evidence is the maintainer's observation of 2026-10-10 (the GPU graph of the task manager while running Wan2.2's I2V in Chrome on an RTX 5070 Ti — between the DiT steps and
in the VAE stage, seams where utilisation drops to 0 appear periodically. With more frames each step takes longer and the seams become relatively less frequent). gpu-lab's
JSON (`outputs/bench-browser/wan-browser-2026-10-10T14-11-07.191Z.json`, not tracked by git) holds only the stage durations and cannot separate the seams. On the development machine
(Deno, RTX 3080 Ti, about 12 s per pass) the seams are 0.5 s or less, and the utilisation trough was 84%. The shape of the DiT loop is
`runWanDenoise` in `packages/models/src/wan/dit-loop.ts` (1 step = 2 serial passes uncond → cond; per pass it uploads the context
([1, 512, 4096] f32, 8 MiB), RoPE and tokens to `session.run`, reads the output back and does unpatchify → CFG → UniPC → patchify on the host).

| Status | ID   | Candidate                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Preconditions / kill criterion                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------ | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ❌     | H-37 | Seams in Wan's DiT passes (re-uploads, readbacks, CFG / UniPC on the host). Candidates ① queue uncond / cond back to back and read back once ② keep the context and RoPE, which do not change between steps, resident ③ move CFG / UniPC to the GPU (the same form as anima's H-33). For the VAE stage the tile stitching was measured (the per-tile readback is included in the tile's interval and not separated — the estimate from byte counts is in research) | **Rejected (measured 2026-10-15 — [research](research/2026-10-15-wan-dit-seams-h37.md))**: with the practical preset, T2V, 1280×704 at 33 / 121 frames, the estimated total of the seams (per-pass uploads, readbacks, host patchify / unpatchify / CFG / UniPC / finiteness checks) is 0.34 to 1.30% of a step (after the in-generation correction; Deno on RTX 3080 Ti and Chrome on RTX 5070 Ti, once each; Chrome's 121 frames is 0.72% by conversion), far below the kill line of 5%. Almost all of a step is the time of the 2 runs (forwards). The VAE stitching is also 0.76 to 1.14% of the VAE stage. Even with all 3 candidates, at most about 1.3% of a step can be taken (estimate), and ③ comes with rebuilding the sha rows. Condition to resume = when the forward gets much faster and the share of the seams approaches 5% (measurable with the same tools) |

## 2026-10-11 attention row-block budget (capacity — ADR 0124)

The evidence is the maintainer's ruling 6 = a (2026-10-11) and ADR [0124](decisions/0124-attention-row-block-budget.md). On the development machine (RTX 3080 Ti, 12,288 MiB),
Wan2.2's 1280×704×121 (practical preset) has a VRAM peak of 11,361 MiB in the DiT stage and about 0.9 GiB of headroom (ADR 0121 — measured). Splitting the row blocks
more finely than the binding limit shrinks the momentary temporaries of attention. It is bit-identical, so it is not a numerics option but a resource policy (the maintainer chooses the trade between speed and capacity).

| ------ | ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ✅     | L-25 | Lower the momentary VRAM peak of attention with `SessionOptions.attentionRowBlockMaxBytes` (the cap per row-block temporary = min(binding limit, budget), output bit-identical). The runtime knob and the estimate are in (ADR 0124). Adopted as a runtime opt-in; no Wan default and no models hook | Step 4b measurement (2026-10-11, RTX 3080 Ti, Deno, the practical preset of the Wan2.2 DiT at 121 frames — [research 2026-10-11](research/2026-10-11-row-block-budget-stage-4b.md), the opt-in `KARUME_WAN_TI2V_ROW_BLOCK_PROBE=1` of `packages/models/tests/e2e_wan_ti2v_dit_test.ts`): with no budget / 1 GiB / 512 MiB / 256 MiB, backing 5.97 / 4.99 / 4.51 / 4.33 GiB, VRAM peak of the whole GPU 11,308 / 10,304 / 9,811 / 9,622 MiB (monotonically down). The total GPU time of the measurement mode is 37.3 / 35.8 / 36.3 / 46.6 s (1 GiB and 512 MiB within the noise; 256 MiB is +24.9%, almost all of the increase in `attention_pv`). The per-stage GPU time is material for the preconditions of the fast path of online softmax (outside the boundary of ADR 0124 decision 9), in the same research. Chrome's point is not measured. **Ruling 39 = a (the maintainer 2026-10-11)**: not put into Wan's default, and no hook is added to models (`WanTi2vPipeline`) or gpu-lab either (121 frames fit in the 12 GiB class without a budget, so there is no problem to solve; the cost in wall clock could not be ruled out — the section on the results of step 4b of ADR 0124). ## 2026-10-23 FlashAttention-2 recon for the Wan DiT (subgroups / workgroup storage)

The evidence is the [recon](research/2026-10-23-flash-attention-webgpu-recon.md) (web sweep + probes + two measurements on the RTX 3080 Ti, Node + Dawn): one DiT forward at S = 27,280 (practical preset)
is 24.2 s of GPU time, the three attention kernels 64% of it and ② row statistics 16.4%; ①QK runs at 32 TOPS and ③PV at 19 TOPS against a measured dp4a ceiling of 65 TOPS, so both are compute-bound and the S round trip
mostly hides behind arithmetic. Subgroup matrix (the matrix units) is exposed only behind Dawn's `allow_unsafe_apis` / Chrome's `--enable-unsafe-webgpu` and the proposal is Draft.

## 2026-10-23 Wan2.2 VAE decoder (from the maintainer's observation that the VAE stage is too slow)

The evidence is the [recon](research/2026-10-23-wan22-vae-recon.md): one next chunk of the tiled decoder is 562 ms of GPU time on the RTX 3080 Ti, 85% in `conv3d` running at 8.7 TFLOP/s
(the level of this machine's f32 GEMM skeleton — the same day's sweep), and the 16-latent tiles with overlap 4 compute 2.04× the output pixels at 1280×704. Candidates in the order of
expected gain; V-1 and V-2 compose.

| Status | ID  | Candidate                                                                                                                                                                                              | Preconditions / kill criterion                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------ | --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ✅     | V-1 | conv3d with int8 activations (per-pixel scales over the im2col row, the dp4a tile skeleton, f16 weights quantised per output channel) — the VAE counterpart of `linearCompute: "a8"`                 | Filed 2026-10-23; the maintainer's ruling the same day: V-1 first, then V-2. **Done 2026-10-23 (ADR [0133](decisions/0133-conv3d-w8a8.md))**: `convCompute: "a8"` — the input quantised once per input pixel over its channels, one exact i32 dot product per tap with one fma per tap (class E, TS mirror at atol = 0), the weight reordered to tap-major on the host at Session construction (reading the canonical layout in place measured 2.3× slower). Spike on the RTX 3080 Ti: ×2.6 / ×2.5 / ×2.2 on the 1024 / 512 / 256-channel 3×3×3 layers (kill line ×2.0), ×0.8 on the 1×1×1 layers (the transposed copy — the fused quantiser is the open point). The maintainer's visual check (8 clips at 1280×704×33, 50 steps, side by side with the online preset — "identical") passed the same day and **`i8-a8-attn8-online-conv8` became Wan2.2's default** (VAE stage of a 33-frame clip 168 → 87 s, the clip 611 → 533 s) |

## 2026-10-24 Wan2.2 DiT in Chrome (from the per-kernel GPU timing on the RTX 5070 Ti)

The evidence is the [research of 2026-10-24](research/2026-10-24-wan22-chrome-kernel-breakdown.md): one 33-frame DiT forward in Chrome is 2,605 ms of GPU
time — linear 41.5% (about 64 TOPS), attention_online 39.4% (about 22.5 TOPS), and small ops (elementwise,
strided copies, quantize, norms) about 17%. In isolation the online attention kernel is 1.15–1.5× slower
than the s16 route in Chrome, while it is 1.1–1.4× faster under Node on the RTX 3080 Ti. K-7's rejection
was measured on anima and Irodori (under the 1% line); on the Wan DiT the same kind of fusion is a
measured 7% of the GPU time, so these rows are filed for Wan.

| Status | ID | Candidate | Preconditions / kill criterion |
| ------ | --- | --------- | ------------------------------ |

Bit-identical; every Wan sha256 row and Irodori's WAV rows unchanged. Node, RTX 3080 Ti, four 17-frame forwards: the fused groups 977 → 471 ms, DiT GPU total 7,007 → 6,677 ms (−4.7%, linear and attention drifted up in the warmer second run). Decision line (K-7's −1% of the total GPU) passed. The pair-form RoPE also fires on Wan2.1 (60) and Irodori (23 + 15). Chrome 155 / D3D12 on the RTX 5070 Ti (2026-10-25, ([5070 Ti record](research/2026-10-25-speed-recon-5070ti.md) §5)): both scenario hashes unchanged (bit-identical on D3D12); 33f DiT forward 2,604.9 → 2,383.3 ms (×0.915), dispatches 2,827 → 2,043, the fused groups 392.0 → 171.5 ms; request 327.3 → 304.6 s (−22.7 s, −6.9%) |

## 2026-10-25 Speed recon on the RTX 3080 Ti (answer-checked on the RTX 5070 Ti)

The evidence is the [research of 2026-10-25](research/2026-10-25-speed-recon-3080ti.md) (three rounds of lenses, each
adversarially verified; Node and Chromium 156 on the RTX 3080 Ti). Chromium-Linux and Node agree within 1% on both
attention routes, so F-2's inversion comes from D3D12 or Blackwell, not from Chrome. Kernel and host gains are measured on the
3080 Ti unless a row says otherwise; S-1 to S-4 are literature figures and arithmetic on the existing 5070 Ti records, and
every 5070 Ti value in the filing text was an estimate; the runbook in `outputs/diag/perf-recon-2026-10-24/runbook/` ran there on 2026-10-25
([5070 Ti record](research/2026-10-25-speed-recon-5070ti.md)), and each row's last note carries the measured value. "Bit-identical"
means 0 differing words on Vulkan/NVIDIA. On D3D12 (Chrome 155, RTX 5070 Ti) every rewrite the answer check measured is
bit-identical too — the K-84 forms, K-85's skeleton (linear, s16, conv3d), F-1 end to end, the F-3 / F-4 / F-6 / F-8 / K-87
kernels, V-5 / V-6 / V-7 / C4 in the VAE graphs, CF-1 and C1a (K-88), V-10, K-86 / K-89 / K-63 / K-64 and LD-1 / LD-3 —
except the fused2 contraction probe (bit-equal on D3D12 but not on Vulkan, so FMA contraction differs between the backends)
and V-8, which changes numbers by design. Metal is unchecked. Every WGSL form below keeps the `gemm.ts:823`
MUST (no dynamic-index component writes into workgroup vectors); round 1's faster-looking forms that broke it were
replaced by compliant forms: the attention and i8a8 forms are as fast as round 1's, while the compliant f32 GEMM form
(K-88) gives up the switch-free B store's ×1.10–1.27 (gemma4 TTFT ×1.21 instead of ×1.28).

Status notes on existing rows (no status changed here — rulings pending):
F-2: the route stays open; the online kernel itself gains ×1.48 (K-84), and the s16 kernels ×1.44 / ×1.58 (K-85).
F-3: measured as A1, A2 and A4 (q/k and cross-q prologue fused with norm, RoPE, permute and per-head quantize; O stored
in BSHD; A4 is a trace estimate): −69 ms per 33f forward on Node, −236 ms per 121f forward; the tiled V → Vᵀ (A3) is
filed separately as F-8. A1–A3 take over the attention node's own quantize dispatches, so both a8 routes switch together
(the `buildAttentionOnline` MUST). F-4: −48.6 ms per 33f forward (register-resident quantize with the gelu prologue; also about −1.2 to −1.5 GB
of plan backing at 121f, estimated). F-5: −20 to −32 ms (estimate only). F-6: about −30 ms (duplicate quantize −11.9,
adaLN −11, norm2 −7). F-7: −21.5 ms (trace). P-4 is F-6's duplicate-quantize part (17% of quantized elements; its 10%
line passes). K-63: deform_conv2d as an implicit GEMM is bit-identical and ×4–49 per dispatch; BiRefNet-HR 1024 wall
×3.4. K-64: generalised by grid-aware conv1d tiles (sbv2 −35 ms GPU per sentence). K-72: its 5% revival line is met
at 33 frames only (cache zeroing is 5.0% of a tile at base, 9.2% after V-5 + V-6, but 1.1–1.4% at 121 frames); the
absolute saving is −3.5 s per request at both lengths. K-79: its precondition holds (all 109 initializers of
vae_decoder_first are byte-identical to vae_decoder_next's; about −0.98 s per request on the 5070 Ti from its record's
build stats, −0.5 GiB; a borrower-side layout assertion is advised). V-3: f16 FMA is 1:1 with f32 on GA102
(measured), so its premise fails on Ampere. V-4: the 25% host share is not reproduced on Linux (2.5% Chromium, 5–6%
Node). K-77: under its kill line (1.5%). H-4: sbv2 residency measured at 646–717 → 104–107 ms per sentence. H-29: the
fixed 128-dispatch chunk cap (not the ramp) measured for decode (H-40); not additive with H-27, and it shrinks MTP's win
(×1.9 → ×1.15–1.43 on repeat text). H-32: GPU top-k upper bound −0.44 ms per token on Node, −0.25 ms on
Chromium. H-34: u32-pair splitmix64 is bit-equal and 5.7× faster (applied per copy — the copies are deliberate). H-36:
anima's text stages resident −2.1 s per image beyond ADR 0112. L-16: item 1 measured (L-26). L-16 / L-17: the host PLE
whole-block re-hash costs 33–57 ms per gemma4 decode token on local-directory sources. The product browser path (Chromium + HF) is
unaffected (a row miss is a 0.20 ms Blob slice). L-14: measured on Node + HF, every PLE row miss reads a whole
33.5 MB part through the scan slot (decode 25.4 vs 10.1 ms per token). Residency (H-4, H-36, Wan DiT residency): on
this machine a sustained-load slow mode (tiled GEMM-class kernels ×15–42 for about 14 s at a time, research §9.3)
makes gap-free all-resident anima slower than per-stage (22.1 vs 14.9 s per image); sustained gains need the
burst-aware protocol, and a smaller submit budget does not help (measured, 7 of 10 slow).

unmeasured). V-3, K-77, H-34, L-14 and H-29's ramp: not measured. V-4: about 2.5% of a tile is left after C4 (indicative,

gains themselves were not measured on it. CFG as one batch-2 GEMM: the drop is confirmed (−0.97 / −0.01 / −0.74%).

## 2026-10-27 follow-ups of the Wan2.2 VAE wave (K-72 / V-5 / V-6 / V-7)

The evidence is the records of the rows they follow: the ADR 0035 and ADR 0133 addenda of 2026-10-26, ADR 0115 addendum
decision 11 and the [research of 2026-10-26](research/2026-10-26-conv3d-geometry-sweep.md), with the material under
`outputs/diag/wave-b-2026-10-26/` (not tracked). V-15 comes from the maintainer's rulings of 2026-10-26 on V-5
(a full Ampere re-sweep now; the per-family case set later — not a performance candidate, so it is in the
[backlog](backlog.md), later; the Blackwell conv3d sweep at a later sitting).

| Status | ID | Candidate | Preconditions / kill criterion |
| ------ | --- | --------- | ------------------------------ |
| 🚧 | V-12 | Choose the axis-reduce split by output count instead of the constant 16 | Filed 2026-10-27 (V-7, ADR [0035](decisions/0035-axis-reduce.md) addendum of 2026-10-26). Bit-identical at every split. Split 8 is 3–15% faster than split 16 on 16 of the 33 shapes, all at P ≥ 8,192 (the largest gap at C 1024, P 8,192); per graph (run 2) split 8 leads on the Wan2.2 next chunk at tile 32 (4.72 vs 4.88 ms), the Wan2.1 next chunk (2.64 vs 2.79), anima's VAE decoder (2.80 vs 2.90) and the Wan2.2 I2V `encoder_pre` (12.08 vs 12.62), split 16 on the default Wan2.2 decode at tile 16 (first 0.62 vs 0.95, next 1.50 vs 1.81). The split MUST stay a pure function of the static shape carried in the key (the addendum); measured on one GPU (RTX 3080 Ti) only |
| 🚧 | V-13 | The conv3d w8a8 quantiser with `pixels = 4` at the 1024-channel input with P = 768 (a static function of (P, Cin) with one branch) | Filed 2026-10-27 (V-6, ADR [0133](decisions/0133-conv3d-w8a8.md) addendum of 2026-10-26 (channel-major quantiser)). Bit-identical (the geometry is in the key). At that shape (10 nodes on the first chunk, 11 on the next, tile 16) `pixels = 4` takes 10.7 / 10.6 µs by median against 20.4 / 20.2 µs for the adopted 16 (two runs, `outputs/diag/wave-b-2026-10-26/v6/table.md`); on none of the other 25 shapes is 4 faster than 16. The addendum estimates about 0.1 ms per chunk |
| 🚧 | V-14 | conv3d sweep coverage: the scalar store, the 3×1×1 time convolution, devices with a small storage binding limit | Filed 2026-10-27 (V-5, [research](research/2026-10-26-conv3d-geometry-sweep.md) §6). The scalar store (output pixel count P % 4 ≠ 0) has no sweep case — every case and every decoder shape takes the vec4 store; the 3×1×1 time convolution (Cout 2048 × Cin 1024, two nodes per next chunk; 28.99 of the 4,162.6 GF of conv3d work per next chunk at tile 16) has none either. Both run the adopted geometry unmeasured (bit-identical by construction, ADR 0133 decision 1). Two tile-32 cases bind a 256 MiB output buffer (two more 128 MiB): on a device whose `maxStorageBufferBindingSize` is below that every candidate fails on them, so the whole conv3d class stays at the default there and such a device can never adopt an `i8a8.conv3d` from a sweep. New cases move the global `caseSet` (its per-family scoping is a backlog item, later) |

Runbook: `outputs/diag/wave-b-2026-10-26/v5/runbook-5070ti.md` (not tracked). The page is the playground `/geometry-sweep` since 2026-10-28 (its V-15 preset: every conv3d case, the `full` set, 5 rounds, 90 s idle, one merged record). The 2026-10-25 recon there compared three geometries only (Ampere's `tile64x64r8x4w16x8k16` ×1.161 next / ×1.234 first on the chunk graphs, bit-identical), so the best Blackwell geometry is unknown. The derivation rejects the record unless the page ran the code that derives the table. **Done 2026-10-30** (maintainer ruling 42 = c): the whole table re-derived from two full sweeps of the current kernels (2026-10-28 / 2026-10-30, 0 errors, 0 output mismatches; the record paths and sha256 are in the profile's provenance) — `i8a8.conv3d` takes `tile64x64r8x4w16x8k16` ×1.346 over 14 cases (×1.179–×2.351), the i8a8 ③PV ×1.142 and conv2d rows32 ×1.064; GEMMs of 129–512 rows and the i8a8 ①QK return to the default |

## 2026-11-05 Gemma 4 at long context (memory)

The evidence is the capacity estimate of 2026-11-04 (the runtime's estimator over the graph declarations, no GPU). Every
Gemma 4 line stores its full-layer KV as f32 (12,288 bytes per token on E2B, 32,768 on E4B and 12B), and llama.cpp's
default KV type is f16, so per token Karume holds twice that default.

| Status | ID | Candidate | Preconditions / kill criterion |
| ------ | --- | --------- | ------------------------------ |
| 🚧 | K-100 | f16 full-layer KV for Gemma 4 | Filed 2026-11-05. Memory only: decode is latency-bound, not bandwidth-bound (L-10, the K-46 refutation), so no speed gain is expected. **[estimate]** It halves the full-layer KV (12B at capacity 262,144: state 8,837 → 4,741 MiB with the sliding layers unchanged, so its peak with a 128 MiB row-block limit goes 16,447 → 12,351 MiB and fits 16 GB). Needs f16 in the states form (generation-context / state-attention / estimate, the same extension K-46 needs) and a re-export of the graphs, which is worth combining with the graph change for vision. It is a numeric change: a named option under ADR [0058](decisions/0058-numerics-opt-in-contract.md), never a silent default, and it needs the long-context quality check of the backlog first. Kill: the measured KL at long context is worse than the line's acceptance, or the long-context measurements show capacities above 32K are not used in practice |

[Research 2026-11-05](research/2026-11-05-gemma4-long-context.md) measured time and memory up to P = 128K on the RTX 3080 Ti.
The sustained VRAM follows the estimate, which keeps the K-100 figures usable as estimates. Decode is what limits long
context on `i4` and `bf16` (370–382 ms per token at P = 128K), while `i4-fast` holds 24.5–25.9 ms, so K-100 does not change
the speed picture.
